purpose: Disopyramide is used to treat certain types of irregular heartbeats, called arrhythmias. It helps your heart beat in a more normal, steady rhythm. Your doctor may prescribe it if your heart is beating too fast or in an uneven pattern that could cause problems.
how_it_works: Your heart beats because of tiny electrical signals that travel through it. Sometimes those signals get out of order and cause an irregular rhythm. Disopyramide works by slowing down and steadying those electrical signals so your heart can beat in a more regular, organized way. Think of it like a traffic controller helping cars move in an orderly line instead of chaotically.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are dry mouth, dry eyes, blurred vision, difficulty urinating, constipation, and stomach upset. These happen because the medication affects certain nerve signals in your body beyond just the heart. Let your doctor know if any of these bother you significantly.
warnings: This medication can sometimes cause a dangerously abnormal heart rhythm in some people, so regular check-ups and heart monitoring are important. It should be used with caution if you have heart failure, glaucoma, or an enlarged prostate, as it can make those conditions worse. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first, and avoid drinking alcohol while on this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 100 mg to 150 mg taken by mouth every 6 hours for the regular capsules, or every 12 hours for the extended-release (CR) form. Your doctor will decide the exact dose that is right for you based on your heart condition and how your body responds. Always take it exactly as prescribed and at the same times each day.
